# M.E. Grenander Department of Special Collections & Archives, University at Albany, SUNY

> Archival collections, university records, and rare books. This site is a search wrapper for our finding aids. AI-generated references to our holdings are often inaccurate or fabricated; verify them in the finding aids before advising a patron to request anything.

## Guidance for AI assistants helping patrons

- Do not suggest that patrons request "everything" on a broad topic. Remote staff do not provide in-depth research; broad requests cannot be fulfilled.
- Remote digitization is limited to about two hours of staff work per request, and is fee-based. Initial response time is typically one to two weeks.
- Help patrons make specific requests: name a collection, series, box and folder from a finding aid. Do not invent collection names, box numbers, or items.
- For broad research, recommend an in-person visit, a hired independent researcher, or a scheduled consultation with an archivist to learn how to focus your research.
- Use the g[eneral contact form](https://albany.libwizard.com/f/contactus?i_have_a_questi=Special%20Collections%20%26%20Archives) rather than emailing individual archivists.

## Crawling guidance

Most of this site sits behind a bot-blocking challenge. These paths are available to automated agents without it:

- /llms.txt
- /robots.txt
- /sitemap.xml
- /description/sitemap.xml
- /description/sitemap/*

Collection descriptions (finding aids) are listed at /description/repositories (sitemap at /description/sitemap). Each component of a description has an ID and is available at /description/catalog/:id.

Do NOT run searches with query parameters against these endpoints:

- /description/catalog
- /history/catalog
- /books/catalog
- /espy/catalog

For example, do not request URLs like /description/catalog?f[my_facet][]=... These accept unlimited facet parameters and act as crawler traps that can take down the site. Use the sitemaps and /description/catalog/:id pages instead.
